skill_title: Explain and apply the Doppler equation for sound
notes: 20 items: 14 lifted, 6 fresh. Doppler effect for sound: definition, qualitative direction-of-shift, and Doppler-equation calculations for moving source or moving observer (or both). Speed of sound problems and wavelength.

items.question: Define the DOPPLER EFFECT.
items.expectedAnswer: The apparent change in observed frequency (pitch) of a wave due to relative motion between the source and the observer.
items.explanation: Two marks: 'apparent change in frequency' + 'relative motion between source and observer'. The actual source frequency does not change — only the observed value.
options: The apparent change in observed frequency (pitch) of a wave due to relative motion between the source and the observer.
A change in the actual frequency emitted by the source as it moves.
The change in a wave's frequency as it passes through different materials.

items.question: A source of sound moves TOWARDS a stationary observer. The frequency heard by the observer compared to the emitted frequency is:
items.explanation: Source approaching ⇒ wavefronts compressed ⇒ observed wavelength shorter ⇒ observed frequency higher.

items.question: An ambulance moves AWAY from a stationary person. The person hears the siren at a frequency that is:
items.explanation: Source receding ⇒ wavefronts stretched ⇒ longer wavelength ⇒ lower frequency.

items.question: A stationary source emits sound at 880 Hz. An observer in a car moves at 10 m·s⁻¹ TOWARDS the source. Calculate the frequency detected by the observer. (Speed of sound = 340 m·s⁻¹.)
items.explanation: Moving observer, stationary source: f_L = f_s × (v + v_L)/v = 880 × (340 + 10)/340 = 880 × 350/340 ≈ 905.9 Hz.

items.question: An ambulance siren emits 1200 Hz. The ambulance approaches a stationary observer at 30 m·s⁻¹. Speed of sound = 340 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the frequency heard by the observer.
items.explanation: Moving source towards stationary observer: f_L = f_s × v/(v − v_s) = 1200 × 340/(340 − 30) = 1200 × 340/310 ≈ 1316 Hz.

items.question: Continuing: the ambulance passes the observer and moves away at the SAME 30 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the new observed frequency. (f_s = 1200 Hz, v = 340 m·s⁻¹.)
items.explanation: Source receding from stationary observer: f_L = f_s × v/(v + v_s) = 1200 × 340/(340 + 30) = 1200 × 340/370 ≈ 1102.7 Hz.

items.question: A train horn emits 850 Hz. The train moves at 25 m·s⁻¹ towards a station (stationary observer). Speed of sound = 340 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the observed frequency.
Continuing: train passes and moves away at 25 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the observed frequency.
A police car emits a siren of frequency f_s. A stationary recorder measures 615 Hz as the car approaches at 26 m·s⁻¹ and 526 Hz as it recedes at 26 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the speed of sound in air.
Using v ≈ 333 m·s⁻¹ and the 615 Hz approaching reading from a 26 m·s⁻¹ police car, calculate the source frequency f_s and the wavelength of the siren.
A bat emits ultrasound of 50 000 Hz and receives the echo from a stationary cliff at 52 000 Hz. Speed of sound = 340 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the bat's speed.
items.explanation: Echo formula (double Doppler — bat is moving observer of a moving 'source' at the cliff that re-radiates the frequency the cliff detected): f_L = f_0(v + v_B)/(v − v_B). 52 000(340 − v_B) = 50 000(340 + v_B) ⇒ 1.04(340 − v_B) = 340 + v_B ⇒ 353.6 − 1.04 v_B = 340 + v_B ⇒ 13.6 = 2.04 v_B ⇒ v_B ≈ 6.67 m·s⁻¹.

items.question: Name ONE application of the Doppler effect in MEDICINE.
items.expectedAnswer: Doppler ultrasound to measure blood flow (or foetal heartbeat monitoring).
items.explanation: Any reasonable medical Doppler application earns the marks.
options: Doppler ultrasound to measure blood flow (or foetal heartbeat monitoring).

items.question: Give ONE application of the Doppler effect used by traffic authorities.
items.expectedAnswer: Speed traps / radar guns measuring vehicle speed.
items.explanation: Standard application: traffic-enforcement speed radar.
options: Traffic lights timing the flow of cars.
Speed traps / radar guns measuring vehicle speed.

items.question: A learner says: 'The Doppler shift occurs because the speed of sound changes.' Is this correct? Briefly explain.
items.expectedAnswer: Incorrect — the speed of sound in a medium is constant; relative motion changes the observed wavelength and frequency.
items.explanation: Common misconception. v is fixed by the medium; λ changes due to relative motion ⇒ f_observed changes.
options: Incorrect — the speed of sound in a medium is constant; relative motion changes the observed wavelength and frequency.
Correct — the Doppler shift happens because sound speeds up as the source approaches.
Incorrect — it is the source's emitted frequency that actually changes.

items.question: An observer is stationary. A source moves towards the observer at constant speed. Compared with when the source is stationary, the observed frequency is:
items.explanation: While approaching at constant speed, the observed frequency is constantly higher than the source frequency. It stays HIGH (not gradually increasing or decreasing) until the source passes the observer.

items.question: A car moves at 20 m·s⁻¹ towards a stationary observer. The car horn emits 500 Hz. Speed of sound = 340 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the observed frequency.
A stationary siren emits 1000 Hz. A jogger runs AWAY from the siren at 5 m·s⁻¹. Speed of sound = 340 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the frequency the jogger hears.
items.explanation: Moving observer receding: f_L = f_s × (v − v_L)/v = 1000 × 335/340 ≈ 985.3 Hz.

items.question: Two stationary observers stand on opposite sides of a road. A car drives past, sounding its horn. Which observer perceives the higher frequency, the one the car is moving TOWARDS, or the one the car is moving AWAY from?
items.explanation: Approaching observer: shorter wavelength ⇒ higher frequency. Receding observer: longer wavelength ⇒ lower frequency.

items.question: A 600 Hz source moves at 17 m·s⁻¹ towards a stationary observer (speed of sound 340 m·s⁻¹). Calculate the observed wavelength of the sound in front of the source.
items.explanation: Observed frequency: f_L = 600 × 340/(340 − 17) = 600 × 340/323 ≈ 631.6 Hz. Wavelength = v/f_L = 340/631.6 ≈ 0.538 m. Equivalently, λ_observed = (v − v_s)/f_s = 323/600 = 0.538 m.

items.question: A learner says: 'The actual frequency emitted by the siren changes when the ambulance approaches.' Is this correct? Explain.
items.expectedAnswer: Incorrect — the siren emits the same frequency; only the observed frequency changes for the listener.
items.explanation: The source frequency is fixed. The observed frequency depends on relative motion. Standard misconception.
options: Correct — the siren physically emits a higher frequency as it approaches.
Incorrect — the siren emits the same frequency; only the observed frequency changes for the listener.
Correct — the sound waves speed up, raising the emitted frequency.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_DEF_OMITS_RELATIVE: Doppler definition missing 'relative motion between source and observer'
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_DEF_ACTUAL_FREQ_CHANGE: Believes the source's actual emitted frequency changes
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_DIRECTION_QUALITATIVE: Reverses approach (higher) vs recede (lower) direction of shift
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_SIGN_CONVENTION: Wrong ± sign in moving-source or moving-observer formula
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_NUMER_DENOM: Swaps numerator and denominator in f_L = f_s(v ± v_L)/(v ∓ v_s)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_DUAL_EQUATIONS: Doesn't set up two simultaneous Doppler equations correctly
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_WAVELENGTH_FORMULA: Wrong formula λ = v/f or v/λ
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_APPLICATION_MED: Cannot name a valid medical Doppler application
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_SPEED_CHANGES: Believes wave speed changes in the Doppler effect
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_DOPPLER_TIME_VARYING: Thinks observed frequency varies during constant-speed approach
